contexts.text: To put forth the hand, take the dove, and bring it in to himself = to apply and to attribute to himself the truth signified by the dove.

It is a Divine Truth that the wiser anyone is, the more he believes that there is no wisdom from himself; and the more insane he is, the more he believes that it is from himself, thus the more he attributes prudence to his own self.

The reason some suppose themselves not to be in good when they are, is that while they are reflecting on the good that is with them, the Angels in whose society they are, at once insinuate that they are not in good, lest they should attribute good to themselves...
That in the Word there are attributed to Jehovah, or the Lord, evil, punishment, etc., Illustrated. AC 2826:3, Explained. AC 8284.
By not stealing, the Angels... perceive that they are to take nothing from the Lord, nor attribute anything of righteousness and merit to themselves.
Since (weapons) have such a signification, they are attributed to Jehovah...
They who attribute all things to their own prudence, and little or nothing to the Divine Providence, if convinced by a thousand reasons that...
On account of the well of water which the servants of Abimelech had snatched = the doctrine of faith, that they wanted to attribute scientific things to themselves.

They who are not in good, and thus not in faith... do not know what the Spiritual is, nor even what the Rational is in the genuine sense, but only what the Natural is, to which they attribute all things...
The truth of faith... is with those who believe from the Lord, for to them are given faith and wisdom; for these attribute no truth and good to themselves...
Under Angel, see this reference. AC 4295:2.

When the Lord flows in through the inward man with the light of intelligence, and thus enlightens the outward man, he then begins to believe otherwise, and does not attribute what is good to himself, but to the Lord.
They who attribute all things to nature... also belong to the same category.
In Heaven they thus speak and think by abstract things, because they do not attribute what is good and true to themselves, but to the Lord...
Under Avarice, see this reference.

They who correspond to the hands and arms, and also to the shoulders, in the Grand Man, are they who are in power through the truth of faith from good; for they who are in the truth of faith from good are in the Lord's power, for they attribute all power to Him, and none to themselves, and the more they attribute none to themselves, not with the mouth, but with the heart, the more they are in power.
Under the left foot, a little towards the left, are such as have attributed all things to nature, but still have professed that there is a Being of the universe from which are all things of nature...
They who believe themselves to be righteous of themselves... are not among the just, but among the unjust, for they attribute what is good to themselves...

The reason such things come into existence in the vegetable kingdom, is from the influx of the Spiritual World; but those cannot at all believe this who attribute all things to nature, and nothing to the Divine. But they who attribute all things to the Divine, and nothing to nature, can see that every single thing is from that source...
They who attribute all things to nature, say that such things have been implanted in fruits and seeds in their first creation...
If they who attribute all things to nature, and to the Divine so little as hardly to amount to anything, would consider these things...

When judgment is given from good at the same time, they who do what is true and good, and from ignorance, or simplicity, attribute it to themselves, are not condemned, but are delivered in the other life by a method of vastation...
Under Anger, see this reference, and also other quotations in that article.
(Adulterers and those who are cruel) are corporeal and sensual above others, and have cast off from themselves all thought about Heaven; attributing all things to nature and nothing to the Divine...

The learned... are to a great extent sensual... When they are promoted to honours, they live more sensually than the simple, and then they believe it to be a sign of simplicity to attribute anything to the Divine, and not to prudence and nature, and the rest to chance.
Under Appearance, see this reference, and also that article generally.

(Miracles) would have still less effect at the present day, when it is not acknowledged that anything is from the Spiritual World; and when everything of the kind which takes place, and which is not attributed to nature, is denied.

They who, in the bodily life, have made use of cunning, and have devised many arts of defrauding others, and at last, from their success, have attributed all things to their Own prudence, in the other life are addicted to magic...
From mere falsities does he reason who attributes all things to nature, and scarcely anything to the Divine.
In ancient times everything evil was attributed to Jehovah for the sake of the simple...
Its being attributed to Jehovah, that is, the Lord, that He hardened Pharaoh's heart, Explained.
The evil which is permitted appears to be from him who permits it, since he could take it away. So here, the firstborn of Egypt being given to death is attributed to Jehovah...

They are in the stream of Providence who trust in the Divine, and attribute all things to Him; and they are not in the stream of Providence who trust in themselves alone, and attribute all things to themselves...

They who trust in their Own prudence attribute to themselves all things which happen prosperously for them, and the rest they ascribe to either fortune or chance, and few (ascribe them) to the Divine Providence; thus they attribute contingent matters to dead causes, and not to living causes...

To have this or that for a god is to love all that which proceeds from self above everything. They who do this do not in the least believe that anything of intelligence and wisdom flows in from the Divine, for they attribute all things to themselves, and the rest of what happens to them they refer to either fortune or chance...
That evils, punishments, and vastations are in like manner attributed to the Lord, when yet, with the Lord, there is nothing but love and mercy, References.
Thou shalt not steal = that no one's spiritual goods are to be taken away from him, and that what is of the Lord is not to be attributed to self.

Wherefore the simple, who are not able to distinguish between those things which take place of permission, and those which are of good pleasure, attribute to the Lord both good and evil; good, because they know that everything good is from Him; evil, on account of the appearance...
That evil is attributed to the Lord, when yet it is from man, References.

They who, in Heaven, are in intelligence and wisdom above others, from the truths of faith, are in such humiliation that they attribute everything of Power to the Lord, and none to themselves; wherefore they do not make any of their glory and joy consist in having dominion, but in being of service...

When a man believes (that the Lord alone has deserved merit), he sets no merit or reward in what is done by himself, but attributes all good things to the Lord; and since the Lord does it from Divine mercy, the man attributes all things to mere mercy.
There are three plagues which follow those who attribute to themselves the truths and goods of faith and of love. Enumerated.
The more they attribute all things to themselves, thus the more they love what they think from themselves, the more insane they are...
They who are in a state of innocence attribute nothing of what is good to themselves...
He who attributes the honour of a thing to himself, or to his own person, in the Spiritual World, when that is represented, appears like a man with his body turned upside down.

After this state, there comes another, which is a state of conjunction with God; in this a man acts in a similar manner, but now from God, nor has he any need now, as before, to attribute to God everything good which he wills and does, and everything true which he thinks and speaks, because this is inscribed on his heart...

In proportion as a man is being regenerated, or in proportion as regeneration with him is being perfected, he does not attribute to himself anything of good and truth, that is, of charity and faith, but to the Lord...

From this appearance it is, and also from the fact that they are punished when they do evil things, that, in the Word, there are so frequently attributed to Jehovah, that is, the Lord, indignation, anger, etc. Illustrated.
